title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated content was used to clone the likeness and identity of a real, named attorney without his knowledge. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI deployment. It occurred upstream of any service transaction, at the advertising stage on social media, where synthetic media was used to make a fraudulent offer appear credible. The victim had no way to distinguish the AI-generated advertisement from genuine legal marketing, and the platform environment where the ad appeared provided no check that connected the advertised identity to the real person behind it.

The specific failure mode is AI-enabled impersonation, used to manufacture false authority. A real professional's face and identity were reproduced to lend legitimacy to a scam that also made a factually false promise, that citizenship could be obtained without the required exam. The fraud compounded over multiple interactions, with escalating document and payment requests, before the victim recognised something was wrong. The attorney's own account, that over eight thousand fake profile videos have been removed, indicates the operation was systematic rather than isolated.

What is not established is the identity of the perpetrators, whether any law enforcement action has resulted in charges, or whether the social media platform had prior knowledge of the fraudulent advertisements.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx legal resident from the Dominican Republic lost $4,820 to an artificial intelligence scam while seeking help to become a U.S. citizen. Victor Hernandez responded to a social media advertisement for immigration services that promised citizenship without taking the required exam. The scammers requested increasingly more documents and payments through Zelle, including his Social Security card and residency card, until his wife suggested something seemed wrong and they discovered the ad was fake.

The AI-generated advertisement used the identity of real immigration attorney Angel Leal from Miami without his knowledge or consent. Leal stated that his image has been cloned to create multiple fake profiles, and he has taken down over 8,000 fake profile videos. After Hernandez discovered the scam, the perpetrators attempted to extort additional money from him. Hernandez filed reports with local and federal law enforcement and now faces financial hardship. Leal warns people not to hire attorneys based on social media and advises avoiding any attorney who requests payment through cash-sending apps.
